newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says no plan to unseat SanMig chief.
newsitem.headline: Manila says no plan to unseat SanMig chief.

text.p: The Philippine government has no plan to unseat Andres Soriano III as chairman and chief executive officer of food and beverage firm San Miguel Corp (SMC), the Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG) said on Tuesday.
PCGG, state custodian of sequestered shares of companies allegedly owned by late president Ferdinand Marcos and his business associates, holds 48 percent of San Miguel.
The PCCG said in a statement it "squelched speculations" it would move to oust Soriano from the SMC board during its annual stockholders' meeting scheduled to be held on Tuesday.

"As long as management of SMC does not run counter to the mandate of the PCGG for the conservation and preservation of sequestered assets, the Commission will not interfere in the operations thereof," the brief statement said.

A Manila newspaper said on Tuesday the PCGG was soliciting proxies ahead of the stockholders' meeting to unseat Soriano because it was not happy with the firm's management policies. The newspaper said Soriano was also gathering proxies to counter the supposed PCGG move.
San Miguel, in a separate statement, said: "There is no proxy war" between Soriano and the PCGG.
"I'm not aware of any such thing," SMC corporation secretary Jose Feria said in the statement.
Analysts said rumours to unseat Soriano from the San Miguel board always cropped up ahead of its annual stockholders' meeting, but no such move ever occurred.
